name: Light-switched brain electrode grid
subtitle: thousands of brain contacts read through one wire

effects.effect: a material conducts much better when light falls on it

effect: a material conducts much better when light falls on it
how: Brain implants that let paralysed people type or move need thousands of contact points, but each needs its own wire through the skull, and wires break and scar. In this grid each contact sits on a spot that only conducts when lit (photoconductivity); a light beam brought in by a single fibre sweeps across the grid, switching contacts on one after another so one wire reads them all in turn.
obstacle: The switches must flip thousands of times a second without the light warming the brain or faking signals.
why: Wiring limits brain implants; reading many sites through one wire lifts that limit.
real: Searches found microLED optrodes, fibre-reflectometry and frequency-multiplexed recording on one wire, but no photoconductive, light-addressed electrode array for neural recording.
